newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila court rejects Imelda Marcos's travel plea.
newsitem.headline: Manila court rejects Imelda Marcos's travel plea.

text.p: A Manila court on Wednesday rejected a petition by former first lady Imelda Marcos to be allowed to go to the United States for treatment for glaucoma, ruling that Filipino eye doctors were as competent as Americans.
Marcos, 67, said she could go blind if the disease were not treated properly and asked for court permission to see her opthalmologist in the United States.

"The Philippines is not lacking in competence, or knowledge and information regarding the diagnosis and treatment of glaucoma. All the forms of treatment are available here. This is not a cause for boasting; it is merely a matter of fact," the court said.
The written ruling was issued by an anti-graft court which in 1993 convicted Marcos of corruption and sentenced her to 18 years in jail.
Marcos, who is free on bail while appealing against the verdict, needs court permission to travel because of the jail sentence. She had promised to return after treatment.

Despite her conviction, Marcos won a seat in Congress in elections last year. She faces scores of other criminal and civil cases in which she is accused of helping her husband, the late president Ferdinand Marcos, steal up to $5 billion from the economy during their 20-year rule.
The Marcoses were ousted in a popular revolt in 1986 which forced them to flee to Hawaii where the former president died three years later.
